threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still stare at the bus schedules like they're hieroglyphics instead of just checking the app. Everyone else is already on their way.
Last night on the N133, a guy dropped a half-eaten kebab, and three pigeons swooped in like it was prime steak. Never seen them move that fast!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids making a band out of trash cans and old pots on the street outside my window. Only in Reuterkiez.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab stand that opens till 5 AM with a line of tipsy locals arguing about the perfect sauce choice.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local when they know to avoid the 14 bus after 5 PM—it’s like a mobile sauna packed with tourists baffled by Muni.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus with a street performer juggling flaming torches at the stop—only in the Tenderloin can your commute become a circus.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think they can just use Google Maps in Gràcia without a hitch. The narrow streets often confuse the GPS, leaving them lost in the labyrinth.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they say 'Tapas'—it's 'tapas' not 'tah-pas', mate. The locals know how to roll that 'a'!

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the market' refers to Broadway Market and not any of the random pop-up stalls on your corner.
Caught the 333 last night, and a guy was serenading us with karaoke-style renditions of 90s R&B. Half the bus joined in, but the driver's face was pure disbelief.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy fixing his bike while his toddler painted graffiti on the sidewalk—only in Reuterkiez do art and mechanic meet like that.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, it's not unusual to see friends carry a portable grill to the park. Spontaneous BBQs pop up like art installations, no invitation needed.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a local when they don’t blink at a dog on the tracks, but you’ll see the tourists filming it like it’s some anomaly.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a pigeon confidently strutting down the Muni platform this morning, completely unfazed by the chaos of BART delays. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists miss that Gràcia’s plazas aren't just for Instagram; they’re where locals catch up over a quiet coffee, not a full-on fiesta.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their hesitation at the tram stops; they always look for a map instead of trusting the signage.
